source.title: NeuronScope: A Multi-Agent Framework for Explaining Polysemantic Neurons in Language Models
source.authors: Wei-Qi Liu; Yongliang Miao; Hai-Yan Zhao; Yan-Guang Liu; Mengnan Du

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent garbling or truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses polysemantic neurons as the motivation for a neuron-explanation framework and reports the framework's explanation metrics. It does not test capacity pressure, feature geometry, or whether polysemanticity implies superposition.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports Number, a count of distinct semantic concepts associated with a neuron, for each model and layer, both with and without refinement. These values are recorded as findings about semantic multiplicity, but do not test any listed version. The Score metric evaluates explanation-to-activation prediction and is excluded. Qualitative clustering figures and cited results are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes neurons are polysemantic and builds an LLM-agent pipeline to explain them. It reports only its own pipeline's Score (explanation-to-activation correlation) and a Number count of explanation clusters. It does not test capacity pressure, toy-model geometry, distributed features, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. Number is an output of the explanation pipeline, not a measurement of how features are represented.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that NeuronScope produces multi-faceted neuron explanations with higher activation-correlation Scores than the no-refinement variant (gains of about 0.05–0.10) and the Choi et al. baseline. They claim it 'uncovers hidden polysemanticity.'
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not implement or compare against the Toy Models of Superposition method; it develops a multi-agent neuron-explanation framework.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that performance may depend on the quality and diversity of activation samples. They also report Number values varying by model and layer, while values are unchanged by the refinement ablation within each model-layer setting.

fits_no_version.finding: An LLM explanation pipeline assigns on average about 2.2–5.5 distinct explanation clusters per neuron: Llama-3.1-8B about 4.5–5.5; Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B about 2.2–2.5. Neurons were the top-200 by activation frequency in selected layers (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated explanation pipelines describe MLP neurons in LLMs as covering multiple semantic modes. This is pipeline-dependent and says nothing about why the neurons are polysemantic or how features are represented geometrically.

record.problems: The semantic-count results are outputs of the explanation pipeline, not direct measurements of feature-to-neuron or feature-to-dimension geometry. Analysis uses selected layers and 200 neurons per selected layer, chosen by highest activation frequency. The paper itself notes possible sensitivity to activation-sample quality and diversity.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 Score results are excluded because they evaluate explanation-prediction fidelity rather than semantic multiplicity or superposition. Qualitative clustering visualizations and case studies (Figures 2–3 and Appendices D–E) do not measure any listed version's feature geometry or capacity claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, or feature geometry.
No analysis of what causes polysemanticity.
No measure of features distributed across neurons. No SAE.

record.verdict_notes: Number values are averages of HDBSCAN cluster counts over GPT-4o-generated explanation fragments (minimum cluster size 2). These are not neuron-activation analyses. The refinement ablation cannot change Number, so each pair of rows is redundant. Elhage et al. 2022 (Toy Models of Superposition) is cited only as motivation for polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-to-dimension ratio, sparsity sweep, overlap geometry, or transition/regular geometry tests.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or feature sharing.
Does not establish that polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, or assess whether it evidences superposition.
Does not measure features distributed across neurons or recover sparse features with an SAE.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

relation.reason: Polysemanticity motivates and structures the explanation pipeline; no result tests capacity pressure, representational overlap, distributed features, SAE units, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: The framework uses polysemanticity as its premise and evaluates explanation quality and semantic clustering, without testing V1–V6.

source_check.notes: These rows are the study's own method metrics and should not count as superposition results; identical Number values follow from shared decomposition and clustering. The authors-conclusion paraphrase overstates the Choi comparison: Appendix H provides qualitative descriptions, without comparative activation-correlation Scores.
